newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rates unchanged in liquid market.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rates unchanged in liquid market.

text.p: *Reserve requirement cut encourages buying in bills

The Philippine interbank call loan rates were unchanged at an average of 10.8125 percent on Friday despite the liquid market as the Central Bank kept its overnight borrowing rate at 10.75 percent, traders said.
Done rates were wedged between 11 and 10.78125 percent, with volume down to 4.140 billion from 5.094 billion pesos.
Traders said those with money to lend just gave it to the Central Bank.
The market had 14 lenders and 17 borrowers.
"Those borrowing were the small ones with meagre requirements," said a foreign bank dealer.
"There's a lot of money in the system," said another dealer. Banks this week got ten billion pesos from matured T-notes and bills.
Thursday's news that the Central Bank will cut reserve requirements next year by two percentage points spurred buying in T-bills in the secondary market, dealers said.
Demand was up for the six-month and one-year bills.
"But those with bills were just holding on. They're foreseeing rates will drop," a trader said.

Bid rates dipped on Friday in the secondary market. The three-month bills had a bid rate of 11.50 to 11.70 versus the previous day's 11.55 to 11.75; the six months had 11.80 to 12.30 from 12.15 to 12.375; and the one year had 12.40 to 12.725 from 12.60 to 12.75, traders said.
